MQ V9.2 support
Some fixes and code reformating

Hi,

can you rebase your change (and enable on MR, the settings about commit)
Hi, I've checked the checkbox for 'allow commit from members ...' hope it's what you wanted about the 'Enable on MR)

I've tried:
PS Z:\git\wireshark-rok> git status
On branch packet-mq_V92_MultiSeg
Your branch is up to date with 'upstream/master'.

nothing to commit, working tree clean

PS Z:\git\wireshark-rok> git pull --rebase upstream master
From gitlab.com:robionekenobi/wireshark
 * branch                  master     -> FETCH_HEAD
Already up to date.
Current branch packet-mq_V92_MultiSeg is up to date.

PS Z:\git\wireshark-rok> git push downstream +HEAD

is now blocked on the ssh.exe and does nothing anymore

It seems that only the first connect works in powershell command line. 
The 2nd try give the following:
PS Z:\git\wireshark-rok> ssh git@gitlab.com
**PTY allocation request failed on channel 0**
Welcome to GitLab, @robionekenobi!
Connection to gitlab.com closed.
PS Z:\git\wireshark-rok>

Don't know how to handle this

I've changed to manage this through the git-cmd interfgace, and it seems to be better:
z:\git>cd wireshark-rok

z:\git\wireshark-rok>git status
On branch packet-mq_V92_MultiSeg
Your branch is up to date with 'upstream/master'.

nothing to commit, working tree clean

z:\git\wireshark-rok>git pull --rebase upstream master
From gitlab.com:robionekenobi/wireshark
 * branch                  master     -> FETCH_HEAD
Already up to date.

z:\git\wireshark-rok>git push downstream +HEAD
Everything up-to-date

z:\git\wireshark-rok>git status
On branch packet-mq_V92_MultiSeg
Your branch is up to date with 'upstream/master'.

nothing to commit, working tree clean

z:\git\wireshark-rok> 

So, it seems that all is up to date

I tried to rebase:
Merge failed: Rebase failed. Please rebase locally. Please try again.

Ok, can you give me the command ... because everytime I tryx it says to me 'Up-To-Date' and it did nothing for the rebase:
z:\git\wireshark-rok>git pull --rebase upstream master
From gitlab.com:robionekenobi/wireshark
 * branch                  master     -> FETCH_HEAD
Already up to date.

z:\git\wireshark-rok>git status
On branch packet-mq_V92_MultiSeg
Your branch is up to date with 'upstream/master'.

nothing to commit, working tree clean

z:\git\wireshark-rok>

Once you have locally rebased, you need to push the new version to GitLab with 'git push downstream +HEAD' assuming that your on repository is named downstream as explained in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/wikis/Development/SubmittingPatches
Note that the change in packet-mq.c is so big that it cannot be reviewed in GitLab unfortunately (any diff bigger than 100K is not rendered, which is a real problem). Is it possible to split the changes in several commits?

All you say I've done and it always say all is 'Up-to-Date'
Splitting the changes in several commits will request some work (as all theses changes were made during more than one year, as I was not able to push changes for a long time). 

But, I will propose to try:

1 - Remove my personal repository on GitLab, and create a new one to start again from the beginning
2 - Try to split in smaller commits my changes
3 - Try to request merges for my various changes

If you agree with this, I will close again this Merge Request

Question: Do we need to change the settings about commit on the MR every time, or is there a default that cvan be set ?

and then I was able to do a rebase and a push force

Enumerating objects: 84, done.

remote:
To gitlab.com:robionekenobi/wireshark.git
 + ccb73a7bb9...f0a7fec8f6 HEAD -> packet-mq_V92_MultiSeg (forced update)

But if you want smaller commits, I will have to restart from the begining

Can I remove the link for the fork by using the 'Remove fork relationship', then delete my project in GitLab (own repository), and then fork a new one from Wireshark's official Git repository ?
